free_tier.stated: The client is free software with no account and no quota of its own; every byte is counted by the debrid account behind it. The backend is 'added in v1.49' and carries Tier 3 in rclone's support table.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable for a user; the object cap is the debrid account's.

retention.stated: not applicable: a mount reflects the remote's contents live.

egress.terms: rclone does not meter or bill; it reads through the debrid account and therefore spends that account's fair-use budget.

interface_detail: Configured with 'rclone config' -> 'premiumizeme'; authentication is an interactive OAuth token in a browser, not the raw API key, so a headless box needs the token copied in. The backend is read-only.
tooling: rclone itself, plus anything that speaks to an rclone mount: Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, restic, rsync over the mount.
chaining: This is the only direct, first-party path from a plain Unix command to any of the eight services: 'rclone mount premiumizeme:' and the corpus has a filesystem, with no zurg, no shim and no container.

limits.value: none published by rclone; the upstream Premiumize rate limit is unpublished and surfaces as a 200-with-rate_limit_reached envelope the backend must interpret

limits_note: Read-only: no upload path exists in this backend, so a workflow that writes into debrid cloud cannot use it.
binding_note: The client imposes nothing; at 1 TiB/month the binding constraint is the Premiumize fair-use meter, not the mount.

identity_cost.detail: No registration with rclone; it inherits the debrid account's identity. Installing it needs no account at all.

reliability_note: A mount is only as stable as the upstream API; a Premiumize throttle comes back as a success-shaped JSON envelope and shows up as a stalled read rather than an error.
confidence_note: The backend page and the backend table were read today. Nothing was mounted, so the throughput claim is absent rather than estimated.

evidence.proved: 'added in v1.49', Tier 3, and the browser OAuth configuration flow for the premiumizeme backend
the full backend table lists premiumizeme as read-only ('R') and lists no other debrid service

price_per_tb_month: USD 0 for a user; the storage behind it is EUR 9.99/month
notes: Named as a separate record because 'which debrid service has an rclone backend' is a question six of the eight answer 'none' and one answers 'yes'. Abandonment condition: a real-debrid or torbox backend landing in rclone makes this record a comparison, not a singleton.

extras.backend_status: Tier 3 in rclone's own table, which is the lowest support tier for a backend
extras.alternative_route: TorBox publishes a first-party WebDAV endpoint (https://webdav.torbox.app), which rclone can mount as a generic WebDAV remote with no backend at all
extras.shim_route: Real-Debrid reaches rclone only through zurg's WebDAV, which is a separate binary and a separate record
